samples.assessment: Parked-domain traffic router HTML. Creates hidden ad-block test elements, measures visibility, assembles browser/locale/automation/GPU metadata, adds it to an embedded Base64 JSON configuration and posts the result to router.parklogic.com. URL responses replace location; non-URL HTML responses replace the document and recreate script elements. Cookie/reload and anchor-click branches implement router navigation. No credential input, form harvesting, local command execution or phishing authentication relay is present. The decoded configuration identifies dotph-nxd/domain parking. Routing/profile collection is accurately reported as neutral capabilities and vocabulary, not phishing.

MV3 proxy extension. Complete manifest, popup and service-worker sources inspected. Sole proxy permission; on initial installation opens its homepage. User-selected free server configures fixed_servers with a SOCKS5 singleProxy and explicit loopback bypass list; stop clears regular proxy settings. Premium controls open a paywall/homepage. Internal runtime messages request connect/disconnect/status. No broad host/content-script injection, credential collection, external tasking or covert traffic-copy behavior found. Unencrypted SOCKS routing and proxy-provider trust are properties of this product, not proof of malware.

Truncated native .NET Reactor-style wrapper. Recovered fixed-pad stack-string decoder names Cor_Enable_Profiling, clrjit.dll, resource __, mscoree.dll and CLRCreateInstance. Native code enumerates local CLR modules, decodes an encrypted resource in blocks, creates a CLR host and loads an assembly through COM/SafeArray byte-array plumbing. The profiler veto compares getenv result pointers with a static 0x1 string rather than comparing values. Resource __ declares 1,937,627 bytes but only 80,105 bytes remain; the resource key and later resource entries are absent. The missing encrypted assembly cannot be recovered or classified. Protection/anti-analysis is supported; a hostile managed payload is not proved.

GCC/libcurl executable self-submission client. Active main 0x4013a0 opens its own image, reads it, locates [[UNIQUE]], seeds rand, and repeatedly sleeps 30 seconds, creates a random filename, changes sixteen bytes following the marker, writes a full self-copy, uploads it with multipart file[]/node/submit fields, deletes the generated copy, and repeats. Node selection is 1..7; the log suggests remote execution but the response is discarded, so receiver execution is unproved. No victim-file harvesting, persistence, local process execution or received-command dispatch was found. A truncated native CLR stub is appended outside the active PE sections; its profiler-code bytes are data, not a profiler check in the running image. Malware-family words in the filename are unverified. Mutation plus executable submission is too unusual for clean benign training.

Concealed malicious code in an npm utility clone. A seeded character permutation and word dictionary recover Function source, then a second permutation recovers a string table. Tron account memo (reversed hex), with an Aptos account transaction fallback, supplies a BSC transaction hash. eth_getTransactionByHash input is hex-decoded, delimiter-split and cyclic-XOR decrypted. One returned source is evaluated; another is launched in a detached, hidden node -e process, falling back to eval on launch error. A 30-second global timestamp limits repeated invocation. Important activation limit: contract.js exports a function; lib/index.js imports it but its chain wrapper is assigned only to the local exports variable. The supplied package does not automatically invoke the contract at import, and that reassignment does not replace module.exports. Hostility follows from the contained concealed loader, not an invented postinstall/import-time execution claim.

ZIP contains only dist/background.js, with no manifest or other extension members. Readable webpack bundle contains standard Solana/crypto dependencies and a Beagle wallet application: local PBKDF2/AES-GCM mnemonic storage, wallet creation/unlock/export, native-vault messaging, connected-tab approval flows, transaction parsing/signing, NFT RPC lookup, and challenge/JWT-authenticated transaction submission. HTTP bodies send public addresses, signed challenges or signed transactions, not mnemonic/private-key/password stores. The alleged plaintext-password report was an error.message appended to an error string. Sensitive export/password RPC handlers merit ordinary application security review, but this supplied background-only fragment does not prove exposure to untrusted web pages or secret exfiltration.

Recovered the complete rotated string array without executing the bundle (15,986 entries, rotation 314, index offset 0x128) and resolved decoder aliases. Traycer VS Code coding-agent implementation, including generated gRPC/workspace operations, OAuth/token storage, local agent integrations, workspace file access, code modification, workerpool subprocesses, PostHog/Sentry telemetry, and bundled Prisma/Google auth/cloud libraries. Main service authorities include authn.traycer.ai and app.traycer.ai:443. Dynamic evaluators inspected belong to serialization/YAML/workerpool/module-loading dependencies. No separate stealth loader, credential-store sweep or independent exfiltration path was established. One suspicious trait accurately reports commercial JavaScript obfuscation.

Inspected 19,068-member commercial-style WebFlix/Symfony application archive, source controllers, configuration, authentication routes, templates and all PHP execution/obfuscation candidates; no concealed webshell or credential-export payload found. A phone-login controller looks up a POST phone identifier, creates an account when absent, and installs a Symfony token/session using the stored password, with only an XMLHttpRequest gate. This is an insecure authentication implementation and may allow account impersonation; the archive does not establish a maliciously inserted backdoor. Routine authenticated session setup elsewhere shares the old matcher, so it is now a neutral co-occurrence observation rather than a hostile backdoor claim.

remote_recovery.method: HTTP GET and public blockchain JSON-RPC retrieval only; ciphertext decoded offline; no JavaScript, native helpers, beacons, credential collection or C2 commands executed.
remote_recovery.finding: Stage 1 profiles host/runtime and fetches/XOR-evals /stage3. Recovered stage3 and implant collect Chrome/Edge databases, GitHub-related secrets and browser/desktop wallet files, POST collected data to /api/exfil, and implement shell execution, file pull/list, screenshots, remote mouse/keyboard, extension injection, wallet rescans and clipboard/keyboard telemetry. Embedded native helpers implement desktop and input capture; no persistence installation was established.
remote_recovery.current_vs_historical: The second loader account latest Tron transaction has no memo and the Aptos fallback returned no transactions. A prior memo from account history resolved a second bootstrap; it is historical context, not substituted for the current chain. The first current chain also bootstraps the implant directly from its server.
